# Let's Talk Renovation

> Let's Talk Renovation helps Southern California homeowners plan, finance and build home Renovations with one team. Construction is by Mars Construction Industries Corp (Mars Construction CSLB #1138550). Financing is the After Renovation Value (ARV) HELOC through E Mortgage Capital Inc. (NMLS #1416824), a second-lien home equity line sized on the home's appraised as-finished value, so the first mortgage stays in place.

## Service area
Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego and Ventura counties, California.

## Projects
- Kitchen Remodels: layouts, cabinets, counters, islands, lighting and plumbing moves.
- Bathroom Remodels: tub-to-shower conversions, vanities, tile and fixtures.
- Room additions: bedrooms, offices and family rooms built onto the house.
- Whole-home interior Remodels: opening walls, ceilings, floors, lighting and finishes.
- Exterior Renovations: roofing, stucco and siding, windows, covered entries and landscaping.
- Backyard and outdoor living: patios, pergolas, outdoor kitchens and pools.

## Financing: the After Renovation Value (ARV) HELOC
- A home equity line of credit in second position; no refinance of the first mortgage.
- Sized on what an appraiser says the home will be worth once the project is finished, not on today's equity.
- One review of the budget, plans and contractor; the home is appraised as finished; one final inspection when the work is done. No draw-by-draw inspections.
- For primary residences and second homes with 1-2 units, including buyers right after closing (no waiting period).
- Not for full teardowns or investment-only properties.
- Homeowners may use their own licensed contractor; the contractor goes through the same project review.
- Different from FHA 203(k) or Fannie Mae HomeStyle Renovation mortgages, which replace the first mortgage.
- Full program details: https://financemyadu.io/

## How it works
1. Book a call or start the secure online application.
2. Mars Construction scopes the project and prepares the estimate and drawings.
3. The project is reviewed and the home is appraised as finished.
4. The line closes, the first mortgage stays in place, and construction starts. One final inspection at the end.
